findings.explanation: The new IssueBulkUpdateDateEndpoint.post (added by this PR) authorizes the request only via @allow_permission([ROLE.ADMIN, ROLE.MEMBER]), which (per permissions/base.py:43-50) merely verifies the requester is an active ProjectMember of the URL's slug/project_id. It then fetches issues with `Issue.objects.filter(id__in=issue_ids)` (line 1103) using only the user-supplied issue IDs, with no filter tying the issues to the authenticated project_id or workspace slug. A member of one project can therefore read and modify the start_date/target_date of issues belonging to any other project/workspace by supplying their IDs, and the activity log records the wrong project_id. This is a newly introduced endpoint, so the unscoped id__in lookup is newly exposed.

evidence.content:
@allow_permission([ROLE.ADMIN, ROLE.MEMBER])
    def post(self, request, slug, project_id):

        updates = request.data.get("updates", [])

        issue_ids = [update["id"] for update in updates]
        epoch = int(timezone.now().timestamp())

        # Fetch all relevant issues in a single query
        issues = list(Issue.objects.filter(id__in=issue_ids))

findings.suggested_fix: Scope the issue lookup to the authenticated project, e.g. `Issue.objects.filter(id__in=issue_ids, project_id=project_id)` (and/or workspace__slug=slug), so only issues belonging to the requester's project can be read and updated.

findings.explanation: IssueDetailEndpoint.get (new in this PR) reads order_by from the request query string (request.GET.get("order_by", "-created_at")) and passes it to order_issue_queryset. In order_issue_queryset, any value not matching the hardcoded priority/state/label/assignee branches falls into the else branch which executes issue_queryset.order_by(order_by_param) with the raw attacker-controlled string. Django's order_by() interpolates the field name directly into the SQL ORDER BY clause (it is not a bound parameter), so an attacker can inject arbitrary SQL via the order_by query parameter. The new endpoint exposes this unvalidated path.

else:

        order_by_param = order_by_param

findings.suggested_fix: Validate order_by_param against a strict allowlist of permitted Issue model fields (and their negations) before passing it to order_by(), or reject/ignore any value not in the allowlist, so the raw user string is never interpolated into the ORDER BY clause.

findings.explanation: The create() action builds IssueRelation rows for every `issue` id supplied in the request body (`issues = request.data.get("issues", [])`). ProjectEntityPermission (project.py:100-107) only verifies that the requester is an active Admin/Member of the project identified by `view.project_id`; it does not verify that each `issue` in the `issues` list actually belongs to that project/workspace. The code sets `project_id=project_id` and `workspace_id=project.workspace_id` on the new IssueRelation rows without checking that the referenced `issue` (used as issue_id or related_issue_id) is in the same project. An authenticated member of one project can therefore create relation rows pointing at issue ids from another project/workspace (cross-project IDOR), because the per-object ownership check is absent. This is a changed line (the issue_id/related_issue_id assignment now also covers start_after/finish_after) and the missing per-issue ownership check is the authorization gap.

findings.suggested_fix: Validate that each `issue` id in the request belongs to the same project/workspace before creating the relation, e.g. filter `Issue.objects.filter(id__in=issues, project_id=project_id, workspace__slug=slug)` and reject or drop any ids not found, so cross-project issue ids cannot be linked.
